definitions.explanation: A person who frequently acts silly or comical to amuse others.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はクラスのおどけ{者|もの}だ。
おどけ{者|もの}の{弟|おとうと}がみんなを{笑|わら}わせてくれた。
examples.english: My joker of a younger brother made everyone laugh.

examples.japanese: いつもおどけ{者|もの}のように{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}っている{彼|かれ}だが、{実|じつ}は{誰|だれ}よりも{真剣|しんけん}に{仕事|しごと}に{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる。
examples.english: He always acts like a clown, but in reality he approaches his work more seriously than anyone.

notes:
Derived from the verb おどける (to clown around, to act silly) plus {者|もの} (person). The nuance is generally affectionate or light — describing someone who is naturally funny and entertaining rather than someone being disruptive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おどけ{者|もの}のように{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}う: to act like a clown
- クラスのおどけ{者|もの}: the class clown
- おどけ{者|もの}を{演|えん}じる: to play the role of the joker

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ひょうきん{者|もの}: funny person; comedian — more colloquial and affectionate
- {道化師|どうけし}: clown; jester — refers to a professional entertainer or performer role
- お{調子者|ちょうしもの}: person who gets carried away; show-off — can be more negative
